headline: Mistral launches Le Chonk, a 1-trillion-parameter open model
dek: Mistral Large 4 enters preview, and the French lab calls it the strongest open-weight model built outside China (CNBC, Wired, TechCrunch).

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: An open model from Europe
body: French AI lab Mistral released Mistral Large 4 on Tuesday, a 1-trillion-parameter model nicknamed Le Chonk inside the company (CNBC, Wired, TechCrunch).
For now, access runs only through a public endpoint with guardrails. The weights, which let anyone run the model locally, are due in about three weeks, after safety testing (TechCrunch).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Trained in-house, tuned for niches
s3.body: Open-weight means the trained model can be downloaded and run by anyone. Mistral trained it on its own hardware (CNBC, TechCrunch).

points.t: Training used 4,000 Nvidia GPUs in Mistral's own European data centers (CNBC, TechCrunch).
The model is strongest in coding, cybersecurity and finance, with chip design as another priority (TechCrunch).
Open weights let outside experts inspect the model's inner workings directly, unlike a closed model (TechCrunch).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A third option beside the US and China
body: Mistral's science VP Pierre Stock says its GPU count is two to three times lower than what Chinese rivals use (TechCrunch).
For businesses, an open model costs only the compute needed to run it, with no subscription. Chinese open models such as GLM are gaining ground worldwide (Wired, CNBC).

stat.cap: Mistral's valuation after its Series D (CNBC)

items.t: Mistral plans to publish the weights in about three weeks, once safety testing ends (TechCrunch).
The rollout will go through trusted partners and governments, aimed at defense rather than attacks (TechCrunch).
Benchmark results had not been released when the outlets reported on the launch (TechCrunch).

caption.hook: Mistral released Le Chonk, or Mistral Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight model, now in preview.
body: Mistral co-founder Guillaume Lample told Wired that owning a model matters even for US companies, since a closed model may not be available tomorrow. He said the lab targets areas larger labs tend to skip.

French President Emmanuel Macron called the release a third way in AI, alongside US and Chinese models (TechCrunch). Wired links Mistral's momentum to tighter US limits on how American companies distribute advanced models.
